subject: Local residency guarantees — VPC handback and proof of deletion
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@clearwave.health>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clearwave.health>
Date: Wed, 7 May 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify VPC residency guarantees and handback evidence

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are sizing private deployments and need to lock down a couple of items before Procurement can proceed:

1) Residency: we need a contractual guarantee that customer data stored in the dedicated VPC will remain physically in the EU region (no cross-region backups or replication without explicit approval).
2) Deletion / handback: if we terminate or request a tenant handback, we require a precise timeline for a full wipe and a signed attestation that all customer-owned data (snapshots, backups, object store objects) were deleted.
3) Proof: what evidence can you provide? For example, a signed deletion certificate, logs showing WORM tombstones, or cryptographic hashes?
4) Short-term access: during handback can we obtain a one-time snapshot of metadata to support audits?

Procurement will also want to know how long you retain recoverability snapshots after termination, and whether Redwood supports HSM-managed keys so we control key lifecycle.

Can you point us to a sample Annex or language and estimate timelines (both standard and expedited)?

Best,
Sanjay
Director, Security & Compliance
ClearWave Health

[No attachments]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@clearwave.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 May 2025 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify VPC residency guarantees and handback evidence

Hi Sanjay —

Really appreciate the clear ask list. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps:

- Residency guarantee: for Private (customer VPC) deployments we support region-locking. By default, data for a tenant deployed into an EU VPC is kept in EU AZs—no automatic cross-region replicas. We can add explicit contract language that forbids replication or cross-region snapshotting without sign-off (Annex B).

- Deletion / handback timeline: standard process is tenant handback -> initiation -> orchestrated wipe of running instances and KV caches (within 48 hours) -> object store lifecycle purge (within 10 business days) -> final verification and signed attestation (within 15 business days). We can offer an expedited path (48–72 hours for full object-store wipe) for an addendum.

- Proof options: we provide a signed deletion attestation (PDF), a deletion log export (S3 manifest with delete markers), and an HMAC summary of object manifests pre/post wipe that you can verify. We can also provide a snapshot of metadata (file names, object sizes, timestamps) for audit only; it would be a one-time export and excluded from retention thereafter.

- Key control / HSM: we support customer-managed keys via KMS with HSM backends (partner integrations). You can control key rotation and revoke access to make any remaining ciphertext unrecoverable.

Attachments: I attached a draft Annex B with proposed wording for residency and handback (see ClearWave_SLA_Annex_B.pdf). Also included a simple VPC data-flow diagram for ops (vpc-data-flow-diagram.png).

Next steps:
1) Karthik — can you review the proposed attestation language in Annex B for legal compliance?
2) Laura — ops, confirm the standard vs expedited timeline feasibility and whether we can provide the HMAC manifest export as described.
3) Sanjay / Procurement — if the wording looks good, I can send Annex B for DocuSign and create a HubSpot record with the procurement team.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week to walk through examples.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ClearWave_SLA_Annex_B.pdf (pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@clearwave.health>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 May 2025 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify VPC residency guarantees and handback evidence

Sanjay / Marissa —

I skimmed the Annex B draft. A couple of legal notes and proposed tweaks:

- "Region-locking" clause: make the prohibition on cross-region backups explicit and limit exceptions to "written authorization from the customer with defined scope and duration."

- Attestation scope: define what we attest to (logical deletion of customer data as of timestamp T, and removal of access keys, snapshots, and backups held on Redwood-managed services). Avoid absolute language like "irreversible" unless the customer controls keys; instead, allow statement such as "to the best of Redwood's operational and technical ability."

- Proof format: we can provide a signed attestation plus a machine-readable deletion manifest. For higher assurance, suggest adding a notarized third-party attestation (we can offer this as a paid service).

- Retention snapshot window: recommend default 30 days for a recoverability snapshot post-termination unless the customer opts into a shorter window; include an option for 0-day (immediate purge) if customer requires but accepts risk.

- HSM / KMS language: clarify that when customer holds keys and revokes access, Redwood cannot recover ciphertext, and that should be considered equivalent to deletion for contractual purposes.

I'll redline Annex B and send a suggested version back to Marissa. One more ask: include an emergency legal contact and statement of timeline for responding to subpoenas or lawful requests that might affect residency.

Karthik
VP Legal, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify VPC residency guarantees and handback evidence

Thanks — this is helpful. Couple of follow-ups from Procurement and InfoSec:

- Procurement wants explicit "region-lock" contract text and a clause that any change requires 60 days notice plus an executive-level approval clause.
- InfoSec asks for the HMAC manifest approach; can you share an example of the manifest format and how we can verify it?
- Can Redwood provide a signed deletion attestation suitable for our auditors (PDF + signature) and, if needed, a notarized third-party attestation as Karthik mentioned (rough cost estimate)?
- If we choose customer-managed keys, can Redwood confirm the supported KMS providers and whether the key lifecycle will be visible in Redwood Console?

Procurement would also prefer the Annex to be DocuSigned rather than exchanged as a PDF. If you can send the DocuSign link and HubSpot ID, we can start the procurement review.

Sanjay

Subject: Re: Clarify VPC residency guarantees and handback evidence

Sanjay —

Great, thanks for the specific asks. Finalizing next steps below and linking artifacts:

1) I attached a redlined Annex B (ClearWave_SLA_Annex_B.pdf) updated with: explicit region-lock text (60-day-change notice + exec approval), attestation wording per Karthik, and the optional 0-day purge addendum.
2) Operations (Laura) confirms we can produce the HMAC manifest (JSON lines with object path, size, last-modified, and HMAC-SHA256) and a small example is on the shared Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/clearwave/vpc-handback-notes.
3) DocuSign: I created an envelope and will send to Procurement after you confirm recipients. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/clearwave/annex-b-2025.
4) KMS / HSM: we support AWS KMS (customer-managed CMK with CloudHSM backend), Azure Key Vault (HSM-backed), and partner HSM integrations. Key lifecycle visibility is surfaced in the Redwood Console when customer-managed KMS is enabled.
5) Timeline: standard handback flow attestation delivered within 15 business days; expedited wipe + attestation available for a one-time fee, delivery target 4 business days (object store purge + signed attestation).

If that works, please confirm recipients for DocuSign and I'll route the envelope. Happy to schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the HMAC manifest format and sample verification steps.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
